caption: My income changes every month but the rent doesn't. How do you budget when you don't know what's coming?

slides.title:
How I spend my
R14 200 average
month as a welder
Living in Eshowe
slides.body:
Male, 32
Single, no kids
Job: Freelance welder, gates and burglar bars
Average net income: R14 200 p/m (range R8 000 – R21 000)

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Backroom with its own entrance, water
slides.body: The landlord is a customer. I fixed his gate and he dropped the rent by R300.

slides.title: Welding supplies
slides.includes: Rods, gas, cutting discs, a new helmet
slides.body: I cannot work without these. The helmet was R750 last month, no warning.

slides.title: Bakkie petrol
slides.body: A quote that I don't win still costs me petrol. That's the part nobody tells you.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Cooking for one, lunch on the road
slides.body: Pap and chicken, mostly. Sometimes a Kota on a bad day.

slides.title: Black tax
slides.includes: My parents' farm repairs, my sister's school costs
slides.body: It goes first even in a R8 000 month. My mother does not know that.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: airtime and data, funeral policy, stokvel, prepaid electricity, vehicle licence, takeaways
slides.body: Six lines, R2 000. The takeaways were R800 and it was a bad month, which is when I buy them.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R14 200 in an average month. In a R8 000 month there is nothing left and I borrow from my stokvel.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded six months of statements to Beyond Horizon and saw my good and bad months side by side.

The bad months were the same costs on less money.

No bank login needed.
